key_sentences: The clinical analysis relies on plasma metabolomic profiling from public datasets (CheckMate 025), where relative abundance or high/low stratification based on median values is used, rather than absolute quantification in tissue.', 'The study does not measure paired tumor-serum samples to correlate local tissue concentrations with serum levels.', 'The study does not report data for other specific metabolites requested in the gap question, such as Butyrate or other SCFAs, in either human tissue or serum.', \"While the study establishes a correlation between plasma inosine levels and survival outcomes (OS/PFS) in ICI-treated patients, it does not provide the specific statistical correlation coefficients (e.g., Pearson/Spearman r-values) linking absolute concentration values to objective response rates (ORR) or detailed PFS/OS hazard ratios in a way that fulfills the 'absolute quantitative' criterion for tissue measurement.\"]", "remaining_gap_recovered_by_policy": false, "status": "unmet", "useful_material": ["The study identifies inosine as a metabolite associated with improved overall survival in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) patients treated with nivolumab (ICI), based on re-analysis of the CheckMate 025 trial data.", "The study reports that higher baseline plasma levels of inosine were associated with longer median overall survival (33 months vs.

22 months) in ICB-treated RCC patients, but this association was not observed in patients treated with everolimus.", "The study demonstrates that inosine enhances tumor immunogenicity and sensitizes tumor cells to T-cell mediated killing by directly binding to and inhibiting the ubiquitin-activating enzyme UBA6 in tumor cells.", "The study shows that UBA6 expression in human tumor tissues negatively correlates with ICB response and predicts progression-free survival in melanoma cohorts."]}
title: Inhibiting tumor cell-intrinsic UBA6 by inosine augments tumor immunogenicity
